raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-IND-ChhattisgarhAcceleratedLearning",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Topographic challenges and sparse population in forested and tribal areas hinder physical access to senior secondary schools, causing high dropout rates among adolescent boys.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish residential facilities for boys in topographically complex areas and implement a hub-and-spoke model with transport allowance support.",
      "evidence": "in some areas, students face topographic challenges in accessing senior secondary schools, in which case boys are left at a disadvantage."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Extreme weather events including heat waves, droughts, and floods cause unexpected school closures, shortening the instructional calendar and deepening learning losses.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop disaster-resilient school infrastructure, integrate climate education, and deploy digitally enabled assessment and remote catch-up learning tools.",
      "evidence": "vulnerable to droughts and floods due to erratic monsoons and heat waves that can force extensions of the annual school summer break"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Economic opportunities in informal labor and seasonal farm work encourage adolescent boys in secondary grades to drop out before completion.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Expand senior secondary science and commerce streams aligned with job market demand, provide targeted remedial education, and conduct parental community engagement.",
      "evidence": "adolescent boys in secondary and senior secondary grades find it economically beneficial to drop out and take up informal jobs available in the labor market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Severe shortages of specialized Science, Mathematics, and English teachers lead to language teachers instructing STEM courses, undermining learning quality.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide structured grade/subject-specific lesson plans, implement flexible teacher hiring in semi-autonomous composite model schools, and offer continuous need-based training.",
      "evidence": "lack of subject teachers in schools managed by the GoCG has resulted in Language teachers teaching Mathematics, English, and Sciences."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Multi-tiered planning and implementation processes coupled with limited capacity lead to delayed AWP&B approvals, slow fund releases, and budget under-execution.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct financial management studies to streamline decentralized budgeting, deploy a dedicated PMC, and implement multi-tier fiduciary capacity building.",
      "evidence": "multiple tiers of planning and implementation and their limited capacities to prepare and manage budgets often result in inadequately planned budgeting"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Fragmented school management and low primary school enrolment result in multi-grade teaching and high per-pupil operating costs.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Consolidate school network operations into 600 model composite schools (Grades K-12) to achieve economies of scale and optimize teacher deployment.",
      "evidence": "fragmented school functioning have led to multi-grade teaching and higher per-pupil expenditure."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Absence of a standardized diagnostic assessment system and weak analytical capacity at the SCERT Assessment Cell prevent effective identification of student learning deficiencies.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage technical assistance under the IPF component to build SAC capacity, establish periodic state-level achievement surveys, and digitize school-based diagnostic assessments.",
      "evidence": "lack of a standardized system to assess student learning through a diagnostic lens restricts the nodal educational institutions' ability to identify issue(s)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Persistent internal financial control deficiencies and unresolved statutory audit observations dating back to FY 2009-10 increase fiduciary risks.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated Audit Committee, hold district and block audit clearance camps, strengthen risk-based internal auditing, and deploy automated accounting modules.",
      "evidence": "deviations are observed in the implementation of the laid-out controls... unresolved/ addressed statutory observations since FY 2009-10."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Lack of systemic annual procurement planning and dedicated procurement complaint handling mechanisms creates fiduciary exposure and potential contracting delays.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate annual procurement plan preparation, conduct independent procurement audits, and launch an online procurement complaint redressal portal on the SIS-SS website.",
      "evidence": "assessment found that there is no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan... no dedicated mechanism in place to treat procurement-related complaints"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Inexperience of SIS-SS staff with World Bank Procurement Regulations for consultancy services risks delays in selecting key technical agencies, PMC, and IVA.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide handholding support and World Bank procurement training, deploy experienced procurement specialists within the PMC, and utilize STEP for project tracking.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risks related to the IPF component include the inexperience of the SIS-SS to process consultancy services following World Bank Procurement Regulations"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Civil works for expanding model composite schools may cause noise/air pollution, improper construction/e-waste disposal, and occupational and community health hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate standard Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) clauses into bidding documents, implement site screening checklists, and enforce national waste management rules.",
      "evidence": "air/noise pollution in mining areas, dust and disposal of construction waste... Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and Community Health and Safety (CHS) issues"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Inadequate fire safety features and lack of universal physical accessibility in school buildings compromise safety and exclude students with disabilities.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce mandatory architectural design protocols integrating fire safety equipment, multiple emergency exits, and universal access ramps across all model composite school civil works.",
      "evidence": "gap in following any fire safety norms in the schools, (c) lack of provisions for universal access to students and teachers"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Overcrowding in tribal hostels due to uncoordinated infrastructure planning risks worsening living conditions, health, and academic performance for Scheduled Tribe students.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Perform geographic and needs-based infrastructure assessments in collaboration with the Department of Tribal and Scheduled Caste to expand hostel capacities safely.",
      "evidence": "over-crowding of students in tribal hostels, (g) lack of geographic and needs-based planning to ensure equity and access"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "National economic transitions away from coal mining risk worsening local employment and socio-economic conditions in coal-dependent blocks of Chhattisgarh.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Target at least 5% of model composite school developments in coal mining blocks to equip local youth with science and commerce education for alternative career paths.",
      "evidence": "endorsements for clean technology will result in the gradual closure of coal mines... There will be a need for reskilling/upskilling for alternative jobs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Inadequate staffing and technical expertise at SCERT, SIEMAT, and SAC could slow down the development of need-based teacher training and leadership modules.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Contract specialized technical support agencies and consultants under the IPF component to augment capacity and transfer institutional knowledge to state agencies.",
      "evidence": "addressing a few technical gaps that might exist in the current institutional setup; and (b) supplementary (temporary) human resources availability"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Complex multi-agency implementation involving SIS-SS, PWD, RES, and DoTSC risks coordination bottlenecks in civil works execution and facility maintenance.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish formal inter-departmental service-level agreements, joint coordination protocols, and a centralized monitoring dashboard at DoSE.",
      "evidence": "requires the capacity enhancement and further strengthening of coordination mechanisms with other GoCG departments and stakeholders both at state and district levels."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Lack of seamless technical interface between PFMS, Single Nodal Accounts (SNA), and commercial banks risks delays in transferring funds to sub-district units.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted training to banking and administrative staff, establish zero-balance child accounts for sub-implementing agencies, and conduct periodic reconciliation.",
      "evidence": "lack of effective information interface between the PFMS system and the Banking network... increased reliance on the banking network has become a bottleneck"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Collection and digital storage of student and teacher personal data across state EMIS and assessment dashboards expose the project to privacy breach risks.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Ensure digital platforms adhere to national data protection frameworks, anonymize sensitive student records, and conduct technical privacy impact assessments.",
      "evidence": "Operation’s activities involving collection, storage, usage, and/or processing of Personal Data are carried out with due regard to the Borrower’s existing legal framework"
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Topographic challenges and sparse population in forested and tribal areas hinder physical access to senior secondary schools, causing high dropout rates among adolescent boys.
risks.mitigation: Establish residential facilities for boys in topographically complex areas and implement a hub-and-spoke model with transport allowance support.
risks.evidence: in some areas, students face topographic challenges in accessing senior secondary schools, in which case boys are left at a disadvantage.

risks.description: Extreme weather events including heat waves, droughts, and floods cause unexpected school closures, shortening the instructional calendar and deepening learning losses.
risks.mitigation: Develop disaster-resilient school infrastructure, integrate climate education, and deploy digitally enabled assessment and remote catch-up learning tools.
risks.evidence: vulnerable to droughts and floods due to erratic monsoons and heat waves that can force extensions of the annual school summer break

risks.description: Economic opportunities in informal labor and seasonal farm work encourage adolescent boys in secondary grades to drop out before completion.
risks.mitigation: Expand senior secondary science and commerce streams aligned with job market demand, provide targeted remedial education, and conduct parental community engagement.
risks.evidence: adolescent boys in secondary and senior secondary grades find it economically beneficial to drop out and take up informal jobs available in the labor market.

risks.mitigation: Provide structured grade/subject-specific lesson plans, implement flexible teacher hiring in semi-autonomous composite model schools, and offer continuous need-based training.
risks.evidence: lack of subject teachers in schools managed by the GoCG has resulted in Language teachers teaching Mathematics, English, and Sciences.

risks.mitigation: Conduct financial management studies to streamline decentralized budgeting, deploy a dedicated PMC, and implement multi-tier fiduciary capacity building.
risks.evidence: multiple tiers of planning and implementation and their limited capacities to prepare and manage budgets often result in inadequately planned budgeting

risks.description: Fragmented school management and low primary school enrolment result in multi-grade teaching and high per-pupil operating costs.
risks.mitigation: Consolidate school network operations into 600 model composite schools (Grades K-12) to achieve economies of scale and optimize teacher deployment.
risks.evidence: fragmented school functioning have led to multi-grade teaching and higher per-pupil expenditure.

risks.description: Absence of a standardized diagnostic assessment system and weak analytical capacity at the SCERT Assessment Cell prevent effective identification of student learning deficiencies.
risks.mitigation: Engage technical assistance under the IPF component to build SAC capacity, establish periodic state-level achievement surveys, and digitize school-based diagnostic assessments.
risks.evidence: lack of a standardized system to assess student learning through a diagnostic lens restricts the nodal educational institutions' ability to identify issue(s)

risks.description: Persistent internal financial control deficiencies and unresolved statutory audit observations dating back to FY 2009-10 increase fiduciary risks.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Audit Committee, hold district and block audit clearance camps, strengthen risk-based internal auditing, and deploy automated accounting modules.
risks.evidence: deviations are observed in the implementation of the laid-out controls... unresolved/ addressed statutory observations since FY 2009-10.

risks.description: Lack of systemic annual procurement planning and dedicated procurement complaint handling mechanisms creates fiduciary exposure and potential contracting delays.
risks.mitigation: Mandate annual procurement plan preparation, conduct independent procurement audits, and launch an online procurement complaint redressal portal on the SIS-SS website.
risks.evidence: assessment found that there is no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan... no dedicated mechanism in place to treat procurement-related complaints

risks.description: Inexperience of SIS-SS staff with World Bank Procurement Regulations for consultancy services risks delays in selecting key technical agencies, PMC, and IVA.
risks.mitigation: Provide handholding support and World Bank procurement training, deploy experienced procurement specialists within the PMC, and utilize STEP for project tracking.
risks.evidence: Procurement risks related to the IPF component include the inexperience of the SIS-SS to process consultancy services following World Bank Procurement Regulations

risks.description: Civil works for expanding model composite schools may cause noise/air pollution, improper construction/e-waste disposal, and occupational and community health hazards.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate standard Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) clauses into bidding documents, implement site screening checklists, and enforce national waste management rules.

risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory architectural design protocols integrating fire safety equipment, multiple emergency exits, and universal access ramps across all model composite school civil works.
risks.evidence: gap in following any fire safety norms in the schools, (c) lack of provisions for universal access to students and teachers

risks.description: Overcrowding in tribal hostels due to uncoordinated infrastructure planning risks worsening living conditions, health, and academic performance for Scheduled Tribe students.
risks.mitigation: Perform geographic and needs-based infrastructure assessments in collaboration with the Department of Tribal and Scheduled Caste to expand hostel capacities safely.
risks.evidence: over-crowding of students in tribal hostels, (g) lack of geographic and needs-based planning to ensure equity and access

risks.evidence: endorsements for clean technology will result in the gradual closure of coal mines... There will be a need for reskilling/upskilling for alternative jobs.
